topic: Water stored in ringwoodite deep in Earth's mantle
hook: This ocean hides a second ocean.
script: This ocean hides a second ocean. Hundreds of miles under your feet, scientists found water locked inside a blue mineral called ringwoodite. You can't swim in it. The water is trapped inside the crystal itself, squeezed by heat and crushing pressure. In 2014, a tiny diamond from Brazil carried a piece of this mineral to the surface, and it held water. If the whole layer is like that, it could hold as much water as our oceans, or even more. Scientists are still debating the exact amount. But it hints that some of Earth's water has been stored deep inside the planet for a very long time. So the next time you look at the waves, remember... there may be another ocean you will never see.

title: There May Be a Hidden Ocean Under Our Feet
description:
Water locked inside a deep-mantle mineral called ringwoodite may rival the oceans on the surface. Scientists still debate how much. Sources: Pearson et al., Nature (2014); Schmandt et al., Science (2014).
